lessonTitle: Cardiovascular Drugs: Antihypertensives, Dual Antiplatelet Therapy and Statins

blocks.text: A 66-year-old man with a drug-eluting stent in his left anterior descending artery stops taking one of his two antiplatelet tablets because his gums bleed. Three weeks later the stent thromboses. Drugs that prevent a heart attack can cause the harm they are meant to prevent, and the skill is to know why each is chosen and where it hurts.

blocks.markdown: Cardiovascular drugs are chosen by mechanism. This unit covers four antihypertensive classes (ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, calcium channel blockers and thiazide-like diuretics), the antiplatelet combination used after an acute coronary syndrome, and statins. All doses mentioned are teaching examples, not prescribing advice.

rows: Block angiotensin-converting enzyme, lowering angiotensin II and aldosterone and raising bradykinin
Dry cough and angioedema (bradykinin), hyperkalaemia, first-dose hypotension, acute kidney injury in bilateral renal artery stenosis, teratogenic
Block the angiotensin II type 1 receptor
Hyperkalaemia, hypotension, kidney injury, teratogenic; cough is rare
Block L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle, causing vasodilation
Block calcium channels in heart (rate and conduction) as well as vessels
Inhibit the Na-Cl cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule, causing natriuresis
Hyponatraemia, hypokalaemia, hyperuricaemia and gout, hyperglycaemia, hypercalcaemia
blocks.caption: Antihypertensive classes compared.

blocks.title: Why ARBs cause less cough
blocks.text: ACE also breaks down bradykinin. ACE inhibitors therefore raise bradykinin, causing cough and angioedema. ARBs act at the receptor and leave bradykinin metabolism alone, so they are used when an ACE inhibitor causes cough.

blocks.caption: MAP is mean arterial pressure (mmHg); P_s is systolic and P_d is diastolic pressure.

blocks.title: Estimating a fall in mean arterial pressure
blocks.prompt: Before treatment a patient's blood pressure is 170/100 mmHg; on treatment it is 140/86 mmHg. Calculate the fall in MAP.

blocks.markdown: **Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT).** Platelets are activated by several pathways. Aspirin irreversibly inhibits cyclooxygenase-1, preventing formation of thromboxane A2. P2Y12 receptor inhibitors (clopidogrel, ticagrelor, prasugrel) block ADP-mediated platelet activation. After an acute coronary syndrome (ACS), plaque rupture exposes thrombogenic material; the two drugs act on different pathways, giving greater reduction in recurrent infarction and, after stent insertion, in stent thrombosis. DAPT is usually continued for around 12 months after ACS, adjusted by bleeding risk. The main hazard is bleeding, especially gastrointestinal, and a proton pump inhibitor is often added for protection. Stopping early after a stent is dangerous.

blocks.title: Antiplatelet versus anticoagulant
blocks.text: Antiplatelets act on platelets and are used mainly for arterial (platelet-rich) thrombosis such as ACS. Anticoagulants, such as warfarin and direct oral anticoagulants, inhibit coagulation factors and are used mainly for venous thromboembolism and atrial fibrillation.

blocks.markdown: **Statins** inhibit HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme of hepatic cholesterol synthesis. The fall in intracellular cholesterol upregulates LDL receptors on hepatocytes, which clear more LDL cholesterol from the blood. Statins reduce LDL-C by about 30 to 50% depending on agent and dose and reduce cardiovascular events. Main adverse effects: myalgia and, rarely, myopathy or rhabdomyolysis (suspect if severe muscle pain with raised creatine kinase), raised hepatic transaminases, and a small increase in diabetes risk. Risk of myopathy rises with interacting drugs that inhibit CYP3A4 metabolism of simvastatin, such as clarithromycin. Statins are avoided in pregnancy.

blocks.caption: Friedewald estimate in mmol/L, valid when triglycerides (TG) are below about 4.5 mmol/L; TC is total cholesterol.

blocks.title: Estimating LDL cholesterol and the effect of a statin
blocks.prompt: A fasting profile gives total cholesterol 7.2, HDL 1.1 and triglycerides 2.2 mmol/L. Estimate LDL-C, then the LDL-C expected if a statin lowers it by 40% (teaching example).
blocks.answer: LDL-C is about 5.1 mmol/L, falling to about 3.1 mmol/L with a 40% reduction.

blocks.title: Monitor and counsel
blocks.text: Check urea, creatinine and potassium after starting an ACE inhibitor or ARB. Warn about the need to avoid stopping DAPT without specialist advice. Advise statin users to report unexplained muscle pain.

points: ACE inhibitors raise bradykinin (cough, angioedema); ARBs spare bradykinin; dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers cause ankle oedema; thiazides cause hyponatraemia, hypokalaemia and gout.
DAPT combines aspirin (COX-1) with a P2Y12 inhibitor (ADP pathway) after ACS to reduce thrombosis, at the cost of increased bleeding.
Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase, increase LDL receptors, lower LDL-C and can cause myopathy and raised transaminases.

questions.stem: Which mechanism explains the dry cough caused by ACE inhibitors?

distractorRationale.b: This is the ARB mechanism and does not cause cough.

questions.explanation: ACE breaks down bradykinin, so ACE inhibitors raise its level in the airways, causing cough and sometimes angioedema.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old on ramipril develops a persistent dry cough. Which alternative best avoids this effect while acting on the same system?

options.text: An angiotensin receptor blocker such as losartan

questions.correctOptionText: An angiotensin receptor blocker such as losartan

distractorRationale.a: Correct: ARBs do not raise bradykinin.
distractorRationale.b: Thiazides work on a different system.
distractorRationale.c: CCBs work on a different system.

questions.explanation: ARBs block the AT1 receptor and leave bradykinin degradation unchanged, so cough is rare. They still carry hyperkalaemia and kidney risks.

questions.stem: A 79-year-old woman becomes confused one week after starting indapamide. Her sodium is 122 mmol/L. Which adverse effect is most likely?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: thiazides can cause hyponatraemia, especially in older women.
distractorRationale.b: She is not taking an ACE inhibitor.
distractorRationale.c: This causes oedema, not low sodium.

questions.explanation: Thiazide-like diuretics impair sodium and water handling and can cause marked hyponatraemia, with confusion as a presenting feature. Older age and low body weight raise the risk.

questions.stem: Why is a P2Y12 inhibitor added to aspirin after an acute coronary syndrome?

options.text: They inhibit a different platelet activation pathway, giving additive protection
They are a stronger form of COX-1 inhibitor

questions.correctOptionText: They inhibit a different platelet activation pathway, giving additive protection

distractorRationale.a: Correct: ADP-mediated activation is separate from thromboxane.
distractorRationale.b: They do not act on COX-1.
distractorRationale.c: They do not dissolve clots; that is thrombolysis.

questions.explanation: Aspirin blocks thromboxane A2 production while P2Y12 inhibitors block the ADP receptor, so the combination reduces recurrent events and stent thrombosis. The price is higher bleeding risk.

questions.stem: What is the primary mechanism of statins?

options.text: Inhibition of the platelet P2Y12 receptor

questions.explanation: Statins block the rate-limiting step of cholesterol synthesis in the liver. The fall in intracellular cholesterol increases LDL receptors and lowers plasma LDL.

questions.stem: Dual antiplatelet therapy increases the risk of bleeding compared with aspirin alone.
questions.explanation: Blocking two platelet pathways reduces thrombotic events but impairs haemostasis. Gastrointestinal bleeding is the commonest problem, so duration and gastroprotection are considered.

questions.stem: A fasting lipid profile shows total cholesterol 6.8 mmol/L, HDL-C 1.2 mmol/L and triglycerides 2.2 mmol/L. Calculate LDL-C by the Friedewald equation (TC - HDL - TG/2.2) in mmol/L.
questions.explanation: TG/2.2 equals 1.0, so LDL-C is 6.8 - 1.2 - 1.0, which is 4.6 mmol/L. The equation is invalid at very high triglyceride levels.

questions.stem: A patient's blood pressure falls from 154/94 mmHg to 124/78 mmHg on treatment. Calculate the fall in mean arterial pressure in mmHg, using MAP = diastolic + (systolic - diastolic)/3.
questions.explanation: MAP before is 94 + 60/3 = 114 mmHg, and after is 78 + 46/3 = 93.3 mmHg. The fall is 114 - 93.3, which is about 20.7 mmHg.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old with hypertension is on a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker and develops ankle swelling. An ACE inhibitor is considered. Compare the mechanisms and key adverse effects of ACE inhibitors, ARBs, calcium channel blockers and thiazides.
markingGuide: ACE inhibitor: blocks conversion of angiotensin I to II and degradation of bradykinin
ACE inhibitor adverse effects: cough, angioedema, hyperkalaemia, AKI, teratogenicity
ARB: blocks AT1 receptor, cough rare
CCB: blocks L-type calcium channels causing vasodilation; ankle oedema, flushing
Thiazide: inhibits Na-Cl cotransporter; hyponatraemia, hypokalaemia, gout
Check renal function and potassium with ACE inhibitor or ARB
questions.explanation: Each class has a signature adverse effect that follows from its mechanism. Marking should reward linking mechanism to adverse effect.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man is discharged after an NSTEMI with a stent on aspirin, ticagrelor and a statin. Explain the rationale for dual antiplatelet therapy and the mechanism and main adverse effects of the statin.
markingGuide: Aspirin inhibits COX-1 and thromboxane A2
Ticagrelor blocks the P2Y12 ADP receptor
Two pathways give additive reduction in recurrent events and stent thrombosis
Usually continued for about 12 months, bleeding is the main risk
Do not stop early without specialist advice
Statin inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, raising LDL receptors and lowering LDL-C
Adverse effects: myalgia or myopathy, raised transaminases, interactions through CYP3A4
questions.explanation: DAPT and statins together address thrombosis and atherosclerosis. Marking should reward mechanism, benefit and hazard.
